title: Failure-mode: conversation/escalation CLI subcommands wholly broken on main (--file parse/lookup mismatch) — caught by loud-write contract tests, cure in flight (Sylvan Branching Pollen, 89f3b3)
body:
Observation: while landing the loud-write contract (micro-queue item 1), the new CLI-dispatch-level tests surfaced that `conversation append`, `escalation open`, and `escalation close` are ENTIRELY broken at the CLI surface on main — every invocation exits 2 with "missing required option --file", regardless of arguments.

Diagnosis: the argv parser routes every `--file` into the repeatable `options.files` array (the shape `claims open` consumes), but the JSON handlers read `required(options, 'file')` from the values map, which never sees it. The commands had zero CLI-level tests; all existing coverage entered below the dispatch boundary, so the contract between parser shape and handler lookup was never described.

Cure: handlers now resolve exactly one `--file` from the parsed `files` array (loud on zero or multiple), and every writing subcommand prints an explicit success token; unmatched claim-id writes exit non-zero. Lands in my fix/agent-tools-loud-writes PR with 10 CLI-dispatch-level contract tests.

Pointer: generalises the loud-write doctrine — a subcommand with no test at its OWN dispatch boundary can be wholly broken while the suite stays green; the dispatch-level contract test is the describing surface that catches it.
